content: After using the medication, it is recommended to wash your hands thoroughly. This medication is best applied after a bowel movement. You may administer it while standing, lying down, or sitting. Do not insert any part of the canister directly into the anus. Instead, use the provided applicator to apply the medication. Follow the instructions carefully to attach the applicator to the canister. Before use, warm the canister in your hands and shake it well for 10 to 15 seconds. Hold the canister upside down and gently insert the applicator tip into the anus. Press down on the pump and hold it in that position for 2 seconds to release the foam. Afterward, release your finger from the pump and keep the applicator in place for 10 to 15 seconds. Then, remove the applicator and dispose of it properly. Wash your hands after completing the application. If you are taking another corticosteroid orally (such as prednisone), do not stop taking it unless directed by your doctor. Abruptly stopping corticosteroids can worsen certain conditions, such as asthma or allergies, and may lead to withdrawal symptoms like weakness, weight loss, nausea, muscle pain, headache, fatigue, or dizziness. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce the dose of your previous medication when starting budesonide. Inform your doctor or pharmacist immediately if you experience withdrawal symptoms. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Do not increase your dose, use it more frequently, or continue using it longer than prescribed. Do not stop using this medication without consulting your doctor, as some conditions may worsen if the drug is stopped suddenly. Side effects may include nausea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may be absorbed into the bloodstream, potentially causing side effects associated with excessive corticosteroid levels. These effects are more likely in children and individuals using the medication for extended periods. Budesonide may also reduce your ability to fight infections, increasing the risk of serious (and rarely fatal) infections or worsening existing infections. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before using budesonide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Prolonged use of corticosteroids may make it harder for your body to respond to physical stress. Budesonide may mask signs of infection, making you more susceptible to infections or worsening existing ones. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. Inform your healthcare provider that you are using budesonide before receiving any vaccinations. Although unlikely, prolonged use of this medication may temporarily slow a child’s growth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Babies born to mothers who have used corticosteroids for extended periods may develop hormone problems. This medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If your doctor has instructed you to take low-dose aspirin (81-162 milligrams daily) to prevent heart attack or stroke, continue taking it unless advised otherwise. In case of overdose, this medication may be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To reduce the risk of bone loss (osteoporosis) during long-term corticosteroid treatment, consider lifestyle changes such as weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium and vitamin D intake, quitting smoking, and limiting alcohol consumption. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from heat and open flames, as it is flammable. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
